questions.question: Round 7's first finding is a flat driver that has folder objects (namespace="flat", parents="explicit" or "implicit"). No planned driver is that combination: RFC-0017 D1 lists flat ones as parents "none" and Graph, HNS, Local and SFTP as hierarchical. Its `stat` cannot see its own folder objects, so the kernel cannot type a folder there without a listing. What should the kernel do with it?

options.label: Refuse it at construction (Recommended)
options.description: `ValueError` when namespace is "flat" and parents is not "none", like the missing-remove_folder check. Then flat implies parents "none", the write-target exemption keys on parents == "none" (BE-008's "no native directory concept"), and the cell product loses a combination nobody occupies. The fake's flat+explicit cells and `test_a_new_key_on_a_flat_driver_with_folder_objects_is_written` go.

options.label: Allow it, stat must see folder objects
options.description: A new driver obligation: with folder objects, `stat` returns a folder object at its key on any namespace. namespace then matters only when parents is "none". The fake's flat stat stops hiding folder objects, and the combination stays in the product as equivalent to hierarchical.

questions.question: When a file-shaped or write-shaped call (read, delete, write, write_atomic, open_atomic commit, the move/copy destination) hits a folder, real wires refuse it in different shapes: EISDIR, EEXIST from exclusive create, Windows PermissionError from open or os.replace, ENOENT, or an untyped error. Today the kernel probes only after a NotFound. Who turns those refusals into InvalidPath?

options.label: Kernel probe on refusal (Recommended)
options.description: After a refusal typed NotFound, AlreadyExists, PermissionDenied, InvalidPath or untyped, the kernel runs one fail-open probe of the key. A folder there gives InvalidPath naming that key. On a write target this runs only when parents is not "none". BackendUnavailable and other refusals pass through. The driver must refuse a folder in some shape but need not type it. This is BE-021's error-path rule, so a call that succeeds pays nothing.

options.label: Driver must type it InvalidPath
options.description: `classify` must return InvalidPath for a folder at the key, on every write and file primitive. Local's driver would keep its `is_dir()` re-check on PermissionError (`_local.py:242`), which puts probe logic in the driver, against D1's "no type logic". The kernel keeps its single NotFound probe.

options.label: Kernel stat before every write
options.description: A determinant stat before put, commit, rename and copy whenever parents is not "none". The answers come out uniform, but every successful write pays a round trip, against BE-021's error-path-only cost rule.

questions.question: BE-030 runs WR-010's metadata gate before the write, so `write(folder, metadata={...})` on a class without USER_METADATA raises CapabilityNotSupported. BackendContract.dfy's `Write` (lines 689-718) has InvalidPath and AlreadyExists winning whatever the metadata is. Moving the gate after them would need a stat before every metadata write. What should BE-030 do?

options.label: Record the departure (Recommended)
options.description: BE-030 states that the gate runs before the type checks and that this departs from `Write`'s order, as BE-031 does for `DeleteFolder`. BK-394 reconciles the model with the first class on the kernel. The code is unchanged.

options.label: Gate after the type checks
options.description: Match the model: a determinant stat before a write that carries metadata, then the gate. A write with metadata pays one round trip on success, and the write still has a race window between the stat and the put.

questions.question: move and copy are gated on which protocols the driver presents, while glob, write_atomic and open_atomic are gated on the declared capability, ranked ahead of the closed guard (your round-6 decision). `docs-src/reference/api/backend.md` says move/copy raise CapabilityNotSupported when MOVE/COPY is not declared. Where should the move/copy gate sit?

options.label: Declared, before the closed guard (Recommended)
options.description: The same shape as write_atomic: an undeclared MOVE or COPY raises CapabilityNotSupported before the closed guard, the key rule and the self-operation check. So `move("f", "f")` on a class without MOVE raises it too, which matches Store, since Store gates on the declaration first. Construction already refuses a declaration with no protocol behind it.

options.label: Declared, after the key rule
options.description: The declaration decides, but the gate sits where today's means check is: after the closed guard, the key rule and the self-operation no-op. Glob and write_atomic stay ahead of the closed guard, so BE-030 has to state two gate positions.

With flat+folder-objects refused, the drivers left are (flat, none), (hierarchical, implicit|explicit) and (hierarchical, none), the last with no writing driver planned (HTTP is read-only). They differ in one corner: a write onto a folder on (hierarchical, none). Keyed on parents == "none" (my wording in the earlier dialog), the routes that stat first (write_atomic by rename with overwrite=False, and move by rename) see the folder and raise InvalidPath, while put, commit and copy skip the probe and pass the wire's raw refusal through. So two routes give two answers for one state, and BE-021's roster ("binds hierarchical backends") is broken there. What should key the write-target check?

options.label: namespace == "flat" (Recommended)
options.description: On the kernel, BE-008's "no native directory concept" means a flat namespace, where `stat` cannot see a prefix. Writes on a flat namespace shadow prefixes with no probe. A hierarchical driver's write primitives must refuse a folder at the key, and the kernel types that refusal with one `stat`, so every route agrees and BE-021 holds as written. parents then governs only folder objects: remove_folder, delete_tree, ensure_parents and empty folders.

options.label: parents == "none"
options.description: As I worded it earlier. To keep the routes consistent, the stat-first routes on parents "none" would also ignore a folder at the target. On (hierarchical, none), a write onto a folder then passes the wire's refusal through untyped, and BE-030 has to record that BE-021's roster does not hold there.

A write under a file on a hierarchical namespace: the kernel types a folder at the key (your earlier decision), but not a file above it. The wire refuses that state in its own shape (Windows ENOENT, EEXIST, untyped), and a POSIX `stat` under a file raises ENOTDIR, which the kernel's two determinant stats take as NotFound. Who types it?

options.label: Kernel, on the error path (Recommended)
options.description: The same rule as for a folder, extended. After a refusal in the probe set on a hierarchical namespace, when the key itself is not a folder, the kernel stats the ancestors fail-open and a file among them answers InvalidPath. The two determinant stats read NotFound as a miss, as `_prepare_write` already does. Only failing writes pay, one stat per ancestor. The product puts 'under a file' on the shape axis and adds a fake whose stat raises under a file.

options.label: Driver obligation
options.description: `classify` must type a write under a file as InvalidPath, and `stat` must return None, not raise, for a key under a file. The kernel stays as it is and BE-030 drops 'the kernel types' for this half. Local's and SFTP's drivers carry it at steps 5 and 6, which keeps ancestor logic in drivers.

questions.question: `delete` relies on the driver refusing an absent key, which an idempotent flat wire (S3 DeleteObject) does not. How should that be handled?

options.label: State the obligation (Recommended)
options.description: `delete` must refuse an absent key and a non-file key without removing anything, in any shape (the kernel types it). The protocol docstring, BE-030 and the dossier say so. The S3 driver meets it at step 2 however its wire allows, and that step decides how. No kernel change now.

options.label: Kernel absorbs idempotent wires
options.description: Add a driver attribute such as `delete_reports_absent`; when it is False, the kernel stats before `delete`. Every delete on S3 then pays a HEAD, which is today's S3 cost, and this PR grows a new attribute and its cells.

options.label: Fix all, one more closing round (Recommended)
options.description: Fix the 8, extend the product with the new axes (refusal shape under a file, a raising stat), then run another unprimed, whole-file and measuring round. Stop if it is clean. If it is not, hand the PR to you with the findings listed.

options.label: Fix all, then hand over
options.description: Fix the 8 with failing-first cells, run the gate and CI, and hand the PR over without another round, stating that the stop rule is not met (an unreviewed fix pass).

options.description: The same rule as for file keys: a first-page refusal in the probe set gets one fail-open stat of the prefix, and a file there (or above it) means an empty listing, or InvalidPath for get_folder_info. Only failing listings pay. The product gains a listing axis.
options.label: Kernel probes it (Recommended)

options.description: list_page must refuse a file prefix, or a prefix under a file, as NotFound or InvalidPath, or list nothing. This is stated in the docstring and in BE-030, with no kernel change.
options.label: Driver obligation

questions.question: list_page on a prefix that is a file: the kernel reads only NotFound or InvalidPath on the first page as empty, so a wire that types ENOTDIR untyped or PermissionDenied makes list_files("f") raise and get_folder_info("f") give the wrong error. Who handles it?
